text:
jamie: morning — eu-west-2 dedicated-pool-2 throughput dipped and p99 spiked around 09:12. looks correlated with tenant-startup running many long-seq beam-search replicas.

ops-bot: [ALERT] eu-west-2/dedicated-pool-2: p99 latency > 1.2s for 8m (rule: infra.latency.p99)

lee: grabbing metrics now. any sign of egress congestion or NVLink saturation?

noah: initial glance: GPU util high but uneven across nodes, PCIe throughput near saturation on node-4, and we see elevated S3 put latencies from the same tenant (lots of checkpoint write).

amy: Ugh. tenant-startup has no burst isolation; they run long synchronous checkpoints after each step which can hammer host IO.

lee: quick options: 1) throttle checkpoint frequency via feature flag for tenant-startup, 2) move their replicas to a less IO-constrained AZ, 3) carve them into a dedicated slice (costly). What's lowest friction?

jamie: quickest is (1) if they accept losing some checkpoints. can we apply a runtime override per-tenant?

ops-bot: quota manager: tenant overrides supported. Example command: `apictl quota set --tenant tenant-startup --gpu-io-share 0.5`

noah: if we throttle IO-share to 0.5 they should still make progress but less noisy. I'll propose a short policy: `quota.io.throttle=ephemeral-30m` to revert automatically.

lee: before we do that can we surface expected perf delta? rough calc: current p99 ~1.25s, target after throttle ~550-650ms based on previous tests.

amy: i'm willing to ping tenant-startup engineering to opt into temporary throttle. also we should add an alert for asymmetric GPU util per-node (stddev>25%).

jamie: go ahead. noah — apply throttle with auto-revert. lee — update the alert and add a dashboard panel for per-tenant IO bytes/s. amy — i'll notify the tenant.

noah: running command now:
```
apictl quota set --tenant tenant-startup --gpu-io-share 0.5 --auto-revert 30m --reason "temporary throttle for p99 mitigation"
```

ops-bot: user noah invoked quota set for tenant-startup (gpu-io-share=0.5)

lee: p99 dropped to ~600ms within 90s of throttle, IO bytes/s from tenant-startup down 48%. nice.

amy: tenant acknowledged, agreed to suspend quick checkpoints for 1h. they asked for guidance on long-term options (dedicated slice vs stronger QoS).

jamie: put long-term options in infra backlog. quick notes: dedicated slice -> predictability but ~+35% monthly infra cost; QoS+fabric-aware scheduler -> lower cost but more complex (owner: lee).

noah: i'll file the cost estimate and a tiny RFC: https://intra.redwood/infra/rfc/8342

lee: i'll kick off a spike to measure NVLink/PCIe arbitration under mixed checkpoint workload; if we can detect early (io spikes + util asymmetry) we can auto-evict before p99 hits.

jamie: thanks. closing loop after we confirm metric stability for 30m and after tenant follow-up. :white_check_mark:
